walkthroughs.body_html:
Performance Characteristics Of Materials — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Performance Characteristics Of Materials brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Performance Characteristics Of Materials.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What property do shape memory alloys have?
options: They glow when touched.
They return to a pre-set shape when heated.
Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.

Producing one unique item.
They glow when touched.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ductility and malleability?
options: They glow when touched.
They mean exactly the same thing.
Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.
Ductility is being drawn into wires; malleability is being hammered into sheets.
